questions.stem: A direction vector of the line through P(1, 2, −1) and Q(4, 0, 3) is:
questions.explanation: PQ = OQ − OP = (4 − 1)i + (0 − 2)j + (3 + 1)k = 3i − 2j + 4k, and any non-zero multiple would also do. Adding the position vectors gives 5i + 2j + 2k, which is not a direction along the line.

questions.stem: A straight line in two dimensions has gradient m. A direction vector for it is:
questions.explanation: Moving 1 unit in x along a line of gradient m means moving m units in y, so i + mj points along the line. The vector mi + j has gradient 1/m instead.

questions.stem: In the vector equation of a line r = a + λb:
options: a is the normal to the line and b is a point on it
a locates a point on the line and b gives its direction
a gives the direction and b locates a point on the line
a and b both locate points on the line
questions.explanation: a is the position vector of a particular point on the line, and adding every multiple λb moves along the direction b. A different choice of a or a multiple of b gives another equation for the same line.

questions.stem: For the line r = p + λ(q − p) through P and Q, the point given by λ = 1/2 is:
questions.explanation: λ = 0 gives P and λ = 1 gives Q, so λ = 1/2 gives p + (1/2)(q − p) = (p + q)/2, the midpoint. Values of λ between 0 and 1 give the points between P and Q.

questions.stem: For the line r = p + λ(q − p), points beyond Q, on the side away from P, have:
questions.explanation: λ measures movement from P towards Q in units of PQ. λ = 1 reaches Q, so going further in the same direction needs λ > 1. Negative λ gives points on the other side of P.

questions.stem: For the same value of λ, the vector equation r = p + λ(q − p) is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: Expanding, p + λq − λp = λq + (1 − λ)p. The form λp + (1 − λ)q describes the same line but gives Q, not P, when λ = 0.

questions.stem: A vector equation of the line y = 2x + 3 is:
questions.explanation: The line passes through (0, 3), with position vector 3j, and gradient 2 gives direction i + 2j. Using 3i places the point at (3, 0), which is not on the line.

questions.stem: The line r = (1 + 2λ)i + (4 − 6λ)j has Cartesian equation:
questions.explanation: The direction 2i − 6j has gradient −6/2 = −3, and λ = 0 gives the point (1, 4). So y − 4 = −3(x − 1), giving y = −3x + 7. Dividing 2 by −6 gives the wrong gradient −1/3.

questions.stem: Does the point (5, −1, 7) lie on the line r = i + j + k + λ(2i − j + 3k)?
options: No, the components need different values of λ
questions.explanation: Solve each component: 1 + 2λ = 5, 1 − λ = −1 and 1 + 3λ = 7 all give λ = 2. The point is on the line only because one value of λ works for every component.

questions.stem: Which line is parallel to r = 2i − j + λ(3i + j − 2k)?
questions.explanation: Lines are parallel when their direction vectors are multiples: −6i − 2j + 4k = −2(3i + j − 2k). In the second option, 3i + j − 2k is only a point on the line; its direction is 2i − j.

questions.stem: The points A(1, 2, 3), B(3, 5, 4) and C(7, 11, c) are collinear when c equals:
questions.explanation: AB = 2i + 3j + k and AC = 6i + 9j + (c − 3)k. Collinear points need AC = 3AB, so c − 3 = 3 and c = 6. Matching only the first two components already forces the multiple 3.

questions.stem: The lines r = (i + 2j) + λ(i + j) and r = 5i + μ(−i + 2j) intersect at the point:
questions.explanation: Equate components: 1 + λ = 5 − μ and 2 + λ = 2μ. Then λ = 4 − μ, so 6 − μ = 2μ, giving μ = 2 and λ = 2. Either line then gives (3, 4).

questions.stem: Skew lines are lines in three dimensions that:
options: lie in the same plane but never meet
are not parallel and do not intersect
are parallel but do not intersect
questions.explanation: Skew lines are neither parallel nor intersecting, which is only possible in three dimensions. Two lines in the same plane that never meet are parallel.

questions.stem: The lines r = i + 2k + λj and r = 3j + k + μ(i − j + k) intersect at the point:
questions.explanation: Equate components: 1 = μ, λ = 3 − μ and 2 = 1 + μ. The first and third both give μ = 1, so λ = 2, and the point is (1, 2, 2). All three equations must hold together, and here they do.

questions.stem: The lines r = i + λ(i + j) and r = 2k + μ(−i + j) are:
options: skew, since the k components can never match
parallel, since neither direction has a k component
intersecting, since their directions are perpendicular
the same line, written in two ways
questions.explanation: The directions i + j and −i + j are not multiples, so the lines are not parallel. Every point on the first has z = 0 and every point on the second has z = 2, so they never meet: they are skew. Perpendicular directions do not mean the lines intersect.

questions.stem: In two dimensions, the lines r = (i + 3j) + λ(2i − 4j) and r = 5j + μ(−i + 2j) are:
questions.explanation: The directions are parallel, since 2i − 4j = −2(−i + 2j). The point (0, 5) is on the first line, with λ = −1/2, so the lines coincide. Skew lines cannot occur in two dimensions.

questions.stem: In two dimensions, |r − c| = 5 with c = 2i − j is:
options: the circle with centre (2, −1) and radius 5
the circle with centre (−2, 1) and radius 5
the circle with centre (2, −1) and radius 25
the circle with centre (2, −1) and radius √5
questions.explanation: |r − c| is the distance from the point r to the point C, so the equation says every point is 5 units from (2, −1). The radius is 5 itself; 25 is its square.

questions.stem: A vector equation of the parabola y = x² − 1 is:
questions.explanation: Taking x = t gives y = t² − 1, so r = ti + (t² − 1)j. Swapping the components gives the parabola x = y² − 1, which opens sideways.

questions.stem: The vector equation r = (cos t)i + (sin t)j + tk describes:
options: a helix winding around the z-axis
a straight line through the origin
questions.explanation: The i and j components trace a unit circle while the k component increases steadily, so the curve spirals upward around the z-axis. Without the tk term it would be a circle in the xy-plane.

questions.stem: A curve has vector equation r = (2sin t − 1)i + (2cos t + 3)j. Its Cartesian equation is:
questions.explanation: x + 1 = 2sin t and y − 3 = 2cos t, so (x + 1)² + (y − 3)² = 4(sin² t + cos² t) = 4: a circle with centre (−1, 3) and radius 2. Moving the constants with the wrong sign gives centre (1, −3).

questions.stem: The curve r = (3cos θ + 1)i + (3sin θ − 2)j can also be written as:
questions.explanation: r − (i − 2j) = 3cos θ i + 3sin θ j, which has magnitude 3. So the curve is the circle with centre (1, −2) and radius 3. The form |r + (i − 2j)| = 3 has centre (−1, 2).

questions.stem: The curve r = (1 + cos t)i + (sin t)j, for 0 ≤ t ≤ π, is:
options: the lower half of the circle with centre (1, 0) and radius 1
the upper half of the circle with centre (0, 1) and radius 1
the upper half of the circle with centre (1, 0) and radius 1
the whole circle with centre (1, 0) and radius 1
questions.explanation: (x − 1)² + y² = 1 is a circle with centre (1, 0) and radius 1. For 0 ≤ t ≤ π, y = sin t ≥ 0, so only the upper half is traced, from (2, 0) to (0, 0).

questions.stem: Which point lies on the sphere |r − (i + 2j − 2k)| = 3?
questions.explanation: The point must be 3 units from the centre (1, 2, −2). For (3, 3, 0), the difference is 2i + j + 2k, with magnitude √(4 + 1 + 4) = 3. The other points are √3, √5 and √18 from the centre.

questions.stem: The sphere S has equation |r − (2i − 3j + 3k)| = 15. The point P(1, −1, 2):
questions.explanation: The distance from P to the centre (2, −3, 3) is |−i + 2j − k| = √(1 + 4 + 1) = √6, which is less than the radius 15, so P is inside. A point on the sphere would be exactly 15 from the centre.

questions.stem: The value of i.i + j.k is:
questions.explanation: i, j and k are perpendicular unit vectors, so i.i = 1 and j.k = 0, giving 1. Treating i.i as 0 confuses it with i.j.

questions.stem: The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for vectors a and b states that:
questions.explanation: Since a.b = |a||b|cos θ and |cos θ| ≤ 1, the size of the scalar product is at most |a||b|. The statement |a + b| ≥ |a| + |b| reverses the triangle inequality and is false.

questions.stem: For non-zero vectors, equality holds in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality |a.b| ≤ |a||b| exactly when:
questions.explanation: |a.b| = |a||b| means |cos θ| = 1, so θ = 0° or 180° and the vectors are parallel. Perpendicular vectors give a.b = 0, the opposite extreme.

questions.stem: Real numbers x, y and z satisfy x + 2y + 2z = 9. Using Cauchy-Schwarz with a = i + 2j + 2k and r = xi + yj + zk, the least possible value of x² + y² + z² is:
questions.explanation: a.r = 9 and |a| = 3, so 9 ≤ 3|r| and |r| ≥ 3, giving x² + y² + z² = |r|² ≥ 9. Equality holds when r is parallel to a, at (1, 2, 2). The value 3 is the least |r|, not |r|².

questions.stem: For any vectors a and b, (a + b).(a − b) equals:
questions.explanation: Expanding with distributivity, a.a − a.b + b.a − b.b, and since a.b = b.a the middle terms cancel, leaving |a|² − |b|². It is 0 only when |a| = |b|.

questions.stem: A median of a triangle is the line segment joining:
options: a vertex to the opposite side, meeting it at right angles
the midpoints of two sides of the triangle
a vertex to the opposite side, halving the angle at the vertex
a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side
questions.explanation: A median goes from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. The perpendicular one is an altitude, and the one halving the angle is an angle bisector.

questions.stem: The medians of a triangle with vertices at position vectors a, b and c meet at the point with position vector:
questions.explanation: The centroid lies two-thirds of the way along each median. From A to the midpoint (b + c)/2, that is a + (2/3)((b + c)/2 − a) = (a + b + c)/3. Dividing by 2 does not give a point on every median.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, the altitude from C meets AB at D. Which condition holds?
questions.explanation: An altitude is perpendicular to the opposite side, so CD.AB = 0. The condition AD = DB describes a midpoint, which belongs to a median or the perpendicular bisector.

questions.stem: A vector along the bisector of the angle between non-zero vectors a and b is:
questions.explanation: Adding two unit vectors gives the diagonal of a rhombus, which bisects the angle between them. The sum a + b bisects the angle only when |a| = |b|.

questions.stem: In rhombus OABC, OA = a and OC = c, with |a| = |c|. The diagonals OB and AC are perpendicular because (a + c).(c − a) equals:
questions.explanation: OB = a + c and AC = c − a. Their scalar product is c.c − a.a = |c|² − |a|², which is 0 because the sides of a rhombus are equal. It does not need a.c = 0, which would make the rhombus a square.

questions.stem: A and B are the ends of a diameter of a circle with centre O, with OA = a and OB = −a. P is on the circle, with OP = p. Then AP.BP equals:
questions.explanation: AP = p − a and BP = p + a, so AP.BP = |p|² − |a|². Both are radii, so this is 0 and the angle APB is a right angle: the angle in a semicircle.

questions.stem: P lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB exactly when |p − a| = |p − b|. This condition simplifies to:
questions.explanation: Squaring and expanding gives 2p.(b − a) = |b|² − |a|² = (b − a).(b + a), so (2p − a − b).(b − a) = 0: the line from the midpoint to P is perpendicular to AB. The condition (p − a).(p − b) = 0 describes the circle on diameter AB.

questions.stem: The point on the line r = λ(i + j + k) closest to P(1, 2, 3) is:
questions.explanation: The closest point Q makes PQ perpendicular to the direction: (λ − 1) + (λ − 2) + (λ − 3) = 0, so λ = 2. Equivalently, it is the projection of OP onto i + j + k, (6/3)(i + j + k). Forgetting to divide by |i + j + k|² = 3 gives (6, 6, 6).

questions.stem: For P(1, 1, 0) and Q(4, 7, 3), the point on r = p + λ(q − p) with λ = 2/3 is:
questions.explanation: q − p = 3i + 6j + 3k, so r = (1, 1, 0) + (2/3)(3, 6, 3) = (3, 5, 2), two-thirds of the way from P to Q. The point (2, 3, 1) is λ = 1/3, and (8/3, 14/3, 2) is just (2/3)q.
